messages:
maria: Heads-up — customer (ACME) reporting 401s only on Safari iOS when hitting their Next/Vercel edge route. Works in Chrome. They say it started after we rolled SDK 1.12.0 to edge bundles.

devon: any chance it's the service worker interfering? Safari's service worker fetch ordering is weird.

maria: yes they have a small service worker in their app that proxies /api/* to our hosted endpoint, so fetch -> service-worker -> fetch to our API. Chrome ok, Safari fails with opaque 0 response then 401 from our backend logs.

ali: can you paste the SW fetch handler? common pattern mistakes are credentials ordering or responding with redirect.

maria: snippet from customer (minified slightly):

```js
self.addEventListener('fetch', event => {
  const url = new URL(event.request.url);
  if (url.pathname.startsWith('/api/')) {
    event.respondWith(fetch(new Request('https://api.redwood.ai' + url.pathname), { credentials: 'same-origin' }));
  }
});
```

sara: aha — credentials: 'same-origin' will drop cookies when target is cross-origin. In Chrome it sometimes leaks due to heuristics, Safari is strict. That can cause missing session cookie -> 401.

devon: also worth checking that the SDK edge bundle is ESM and not accidentally using node-only auth flow. But first, cookies + CORS headers.

maria: they tried credentials: 'include' and still saw opaque responses intermittently. They said preflight returns 204 and then the real request is opaque (status 0) in Safari. backend logs show no auth header received.

ali: status 0/opaque usually means the response is blocked by CORS or network-level opaque (e.g., redirect to a third-party or Service Worker delivered a cross-origin opaque response). Any redirects on the backend auth endpoint? set-cookie with SameSite maybe?

maria: backend has redirect to /login for missing session (302) — that would become opaque in cross-origin fetch if CORS not set to allow-credentials. They also aren't setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials on the redirect response.

support-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026 — assigned to @devon. Please attach repro.

devon: repro steps requested for ACME: 1) Next app deployed to Vercel with SW registered, 2) SDK 1.12.0 in edge bundle, 3) Safari iOS 16.4 on iPhone, 4) login cookie present on primary domain, 5) trigger /api/generate (proxied).

maria: I asked them to try these quick mitigations: a) set fetch in SW to credentials: 'include' and set fetch init mode: 'cors' explicitly, b) ensure backend returns Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <origin> not '*', c) avoid redirect -> return 401 JSON instead of 302 for API endpoints.

ali: another nuance: Service Worker will perform its own CORS checks. On Safari, when SW issues a fetch to cross-origin with credentials included, the preflight must include Access-Control-Allow-Credentials and the final response must also. If any redirect happens, Safari treats it as opaque.

sara: note about SDK: we found a tangential bug where SDK 1.12.0 uses fetch polyfill that sets redirect: 'follow' and relies on Set-Cookie on 302; if the SW proxied request triggers a redirect, cookie flow can be broken. Suggest customer try SDK 1.11.2 (previous) which they confirmed works in their app.

maria: they downgraded to 1.11.2 and Safari passed the request (no 401). So looks like combination: 1.12.0 + SW + Safari redirect/cors behavior.

devon: action items: (1) engineer-side: create a small repro with Next+Vercel+minimal SW + SDK 1.12.0 to reproduce in our lab (I can do this). (2) support: advise customer to temporarily pin 1.11.2 and apply backend change to return 401 JSON for API auth instead of 302 redirect. (3) runtime: add note to edge SDK release that SW + cross-origin cookie flows can be flaky on Safari and suggest patterns.

ali: I'll also run a quick diff between 1.11.2 and 1.12.0 to see what changed around fetch polyfill/redirect handling.

maria: customer accepted pin + backend tweak for now. They've asked for ETA on a permanent fix because they need to upgrade.

devon: ETA: repro + root cause by EOD tomorrow. If confirmed, we'll prepare a patch or mitigation in next patch release.

sara: small workaround doc to share with customer (to copy into ticket):
- If using Service Worker proxying cross-origin calls, prefer to avoid server-side 302 redirects on API endpoints; return 401 JSON for auth.
- In SW use: fetch(url, { credentials: 'include', mode: 'cors', redirect: 'manual' }) and then handle redirects explicitly.
- Ensure backend responses include Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true and exact Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.

maria: adding logs from customer: "fetch to https://api.redwood.ai/api/generate -> preflight 204, follow-up fetch -> opaque response, then console shows TypeError: NetworkError when attempting to fetch resource."

devon: thanks. I'll repro and post minimal repo. tagging @ali for SDK diff results.

support-bot: Ticket updated: #INC-2026 — assigned devon, severity P2.
